name: The very same Munchhausen
description: A positive integer $$$a$$$ is given. Baron Munchausen claims that he knows such a positive integer $$$n$$$ that if one multiplies $$$n$$$ by $$$a$$$, the sum of its digits decreases $$$a$$$ times. In other words, $$$S(an) = S(n)/a$$$, where $$$S(x)$$$ denotes the sum of digits of the number $$$x$$$. Find out if what Baron told can be true.
input_specification: The only line contains a single integer $$$a$$$ ($$$2 \le a \le 10^3$$$).
output_specification: If there is no such number $$$n$$$, print $$$-1$$$. Otherwise print any appropriate positive integer $$$n$$$. Your number must not consist of more than $$$5\cdot10^5$$$ digits. We can show that under given constraints either there is no answer, or there is an answer no longer than $$$5\cdot10^5$$$ digits.
approach_summary: Identify exchange argument or greedy choice property. Sort elements by payoff ratio or deadline and greedily pick candidates to achieve global optimum.
